segments.narration: A dung heap may have started the Thirty Years' War.
Prague, the twenty-third of May, 1618. Protestant nobles put two Catholic regents on trial inside the castle, found them guilty, and threw them out of a third-floor window.
Then they threw the secretary out too. All three landed in the ditch below and got up.
How does anybody survive three storeys onto stone? The Catholic version said angels caught them. The Protestant version said they hit a heap of manure.

That argument outlived every man in the room. The revolt they started pulled half of Europe into thirty years of war, and it opened for real at White Mountain two years later — over a window, and whatever was piled under it.
